item.title: On the square of an isosimple module
item.description: arXiv:2610.26905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S$ be an isosimple module, that is, a nonzero module isomorphic to every nonzero submodule of itself. In this paper, we investigate if the square $S^2 := S \oplus S$ is isoantian when $S$ is an isosimple module. If the base ring is commutative, then the answer is yes. However, for noncommutative rings this is no longer true even when $\mathrm{End}_R(S)$ is a discrete valuation ring. We also give some positive results coming from quasi-projectivity and Morita equivalence. Finally, we consider when every finite powers of an isosimple module are isoantian provided it holds for the square. Our related result says that if $S^2$ is isoantian and $E = \mathrm{End}_R(S)$ is either commutative Noetherian or right semihereditary, then every finite power of $S$ is isoantian.
item.dc:creator: Ran Yan, Xiaolei Zhang

item.title: The algebraic and geometric classification of post-$3$-Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.27300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A post-$3$-Lie algebra is a $3$-Lie algebra with an additional ternary multiplication, skew-symmetric in the first two arguments, related to the bracket by four compatibility identities. We give the algebraic and geometric classification of complex $2$- and $3$-dimensional post-$3$-Lie algebras and of complex $4$-dimensional nilpotent post-$3$-Lie algebras. The variety of $2$-dimensional algebras is irreducible of dimension $4$; the variety of $3$-dimensional algebras has dimension $12$ and $12$ irreducible components, and exactly one rigid algebra; the variety of $4$-dimensional nilpotent algebras has dimension $14$, two irreducible components and no rigid algebras.
item.dc:creator: Hani Abdelwahab, Kobiljon Abdurasulov, Ivan Kaygorodov

item.title: The Finite Basis Problem for Multiplicatively Idempotent Semirings
item.description: arXiv:2610.27463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The variety of semirings satisfying $x^2\approx x$ is hereditarily finitely based in the signature consisting of addition and multiplication, without designated constants. Multiplication may be noncommutative, and the semirings need not be finite. A subdirect decomposition reduces the proof to the subvarieties defined by $3x\approx x$ and $3x\approx2x$. In the latter case, we express each polynomial identity using a common doubled part and isolated word occurrences. Four fixed identities align the first- and last-occurrence words of these occurrences. Induction on their content extracts protected identities. The associated word identities define a band variety, to which the finite basis theorem for bands applies.
item.dc:creator: Aifa Wang, Lili Wang

item.title: Quantum polynomial-time conjugacy in metabelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.27250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the conjugacy problem in finitely presented metabelian groups with a fixed number of generators is solvable in bounded-error quantum polynomial time, uniformly in the defining relations of the group. Both the group presentation and the words representing the elements are part of the input. The main ingredient is a quantum polynomial-time algorithm for computing all multiplicative relations among a fixed number of units in a commutative affine $\mathbb Z$-algebra presented with a fixed number of variables. The algorithm reduces the problem to computations in finite-dimensional algebras over $\mathbb Q$ and finite rings by identifying the lattice of exponent vectors whose corresponding products are algebraic over the coefficient field. An effective arithmetic splitting combines the rational and finite-ring computations. The proof uses effective bounds for polynomial equations, algorithms for finite-dimensional commutative algebras, quantum integer factorization, and finite abelian hidden-subgroup algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Alexei Miasnikov, Alexander Ushakov

item.title: Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.27492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop the general theory of Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories. We prove categorical versions of classical results such as Engel's theorem, Cartan's criterion, and that all derivations of a strongly semisimple Lie algebra are inner. For finite-dimensional graded Lie algebras, we construct a graded category $\mathcal{O}$, classify its graded-simple objects, and prove the generic graded irreducibility of Verma modules. Lastly, we develop the theory of root systems for contragredient Lie algebras.
item.dc:creator: Iv\'an Angiono, Agustina Czenky, Pavel Etingof, Victor Ostrik, Julia Plavnik, Guillermo Sanmarco

item.title: A Lie Bracket on the Space of (Right) Biderivations of a Lie Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2507.12089v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Derivations of a Lie algebra form a Lie algebra under the commutator bracket. Motivated by this property, we investigate Lie algebra structures on spaces of biderivations. We introduce right and left biderivations and show that their spaces admit natural Lie brackets induced by pointwise commutators of derivations. We describe these structures in terms of current Lie algebras and establish a cohomological characterisation of classical biderivations, with applications to semisimple and Heisenberg Lie algebras. We also examine the relation between the right and left brackets for symmetric and skew-symmetric biderivations. Finally, we discuss the pointwise integration of right biderivations into families of Lie group automorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Alfonso Di Bartolo, Gianmarco La Rosa

item.title: Root of the generic cubic as a power series in the discriminant
item.description: arXiv:2605.25992v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An observation of J-P.~Serre implies that the generic monic cubic polynomial, unique among generic monic polynomials of degree at least two, has a root that is a power series in the discriminant; Serre asked for a formula. We give formulas that work over any field with an absolute value and in every characteristic. Over a complete non-archimedean field we identify the root intrinsically: it is the isolated root, the one farthest from the others. We also answer the next case of Serre's question, computing explicitly the distinguished ramified quadratic factor of the generic monic quartic. The methods combine Hensel's lemma, identities for generalized binomial series, and elementary non-archimedean analysis.
item.dc:creator: Jason Bland, Skip Garibaldi, Joel Rosenberg

item.title: Transposed Poisson structure on the Witt-type algebra $\mathcal{W}(a,-1)$: Derivations, Automorphisms, and Rota--Baxter operators
item.description: arXiv:2606.20584v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we provide a comprehensive study of the structural properties of the transposed Poisson algebra $\mathcal{W}(a,-1)$. We classify several types of linear maps, including derivations, local derivations, quasi-derivations, and $\delta$-derivations, showing that non-trivial $\delta$-derivations exist only for $\delta=1$ and $\delta=\frac{1}{2}$. Furthermore, we describe the groups of automorphisms, local automorphisms, 2-local automorphisms, and quasi-automorphisms. We also investigate Rota--Baxter operators of weight $1$ on $\mathcal{W}(a,-1)$. Specifically, we classify operators that are homogeneous with respect to both the standard $\mathbf{Z}$-grading and a $\mathbf{Z}_2$-grading, establishing a rigidity result for the latter case. Finally, we classify all $\mathbf{W}$-compatible Novikov--Poisson structures, demonstrating that the associative product on the Witt algebra is universally compatible with its known Novikov structures.
item.dc:creator: Roman Lubkov, Ilya Shiringovskiy

item.title: The Parafree Conjecture for Lie rings and associative algebras
item.description: arXiv:2608.20570v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a finitely generated parafree Lie ring with nonzero second homology and, over every nonzero commutative ring, a finitely generated parafree augmented associative algebra with nonzero second homology. These examples disprove the analogues of the Parafree Conjecture for Lie rings and for augmented associative algebras. Our constructions also provide finitely generated parafree examples that are not finitely presented, both in the Lie-ring and augmented-algebra settings.
item.dc:creator: Vasily Ionin, Roman Mikhailov

item.title: Sign Propagation of Principal Minors in Fully Semimonotone Matrices and Stone's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.22829v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stone conjectured in 1981 that every fully semimonotone $\mathbf{Q}_0$-matrix is a $\mathbf{P}_0$-matrix; Murthy and Parthasarathy (1995) proved this for orders up to $4$ and for several special classes. We study the principal minors of fully semimonotone matrices $A\in\Ezerof$ without using $\Qzero$. Let $\G(A)$ be the graph whose vertices are the index sets $\alpha$ with $\det A_{\alpha\alpha}\neq 0$ (including $\alpha=\emptyset$), two vertices being adjacent when they differ in exactly one index. We prove that the sign of the principal minor is constant on every connected component of $\G(A)$, and positive on the component of $\emptyset$. Consequences: an $\Ezerof$-matrix with no vanishing principal minor is a $\mathbf{P}$-matrix, and any $\Ezerof$-matrix satisfying a simple ``descending'' condition on its nonvanishing minors is a $\mathbf{P}_0$-matrix. We show that a sign change across two steps through vanishing minors forces strictly positive coupling in the corresponding principal pivotal transform, and that a principal submatrix of minimal order with negative determinant is an almost-$\mathbf{P}_0$ matrix whose inverse lies in $\Ezerof\cap\Nzero$ and has zero diagonal. Explicit examples show that the component structure can contain negative components, that $\det A>0$ does not force $A\in\Pzero$ in $\Ezerof$, that $\Ezerof$ is not invariant under $A\mapsto A+\varepsilon I$, and that $\Ezerof\cap\Pzero$ contains matrices with $\det A>0$ outside $\Qzero$. Stone's conjecture itself remains open.
item.dc:creator: Sajal Ghosh

item.title: A polynomial criterion for Jordan elements in a free associative algebra
item.description: arXiv:2609.08314v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $J$ be the Jordan subalgebra of the free associative algebra $\Q\langle X\rangle$ generated by $X$ and $1$ under $a\cdot b=\tfrac12(ab+ba)$. We give a polynomial criterion for an associative polynomial to belong to $J$. For every $n\ge1$, Robbins' recursion gives a family of operators $T_\alpha\in\Q[S_n]$, indexed by compositions of $n$ into parts $1$ and $2$. We prove that right multiplication by $U_n=\sum_\alpha T_\alpha^\dagger T_\alpha$ has image $\SJ(n)$, the space of multilinear Jordan elements. If its characteristic polynomial is $t^{e_n}q_n(t)$, where $q_n(0)\ne0$, then $\Pi_n=I-q_n(U_n)/q_n(0)$ is an idempotent and $f\in\SJ(n)$ if and only if $fq_n(U_n)=0$, or equivalently $f\Pi_n=f$. The same operators give the criterion for arbitrary homogeneous polynomials of degree $n$. We also prove $\SJ(n)\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n}r_\lambda S^\lambda$, where $r_\lambda=\rank\rho_\lambda(U_n)$. Thus $\dim\SJ(n)=\sum_\lambda d_\lambda r_\lambda$ and $e_n=\sum_\lambda d_\lambda(d_\lambda-r_\lambda)$, with $d_\lambda=\dim S^\lambda$. We give a recursion for the corresponding row spaces and use it to compute the multiplicities over $\Q$ through degree $12$. Exact block characteristic polynomials through degree $7$ and direct computations in small degrees illustrate the criterion.
item.dc:creator: F. Mashurov, B. Sartayev

item.title: A parity obstruction to completeness of object cotorsion pairs
item.description: arXiv:2609.18681v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fu, Guil Asensio, Herzog and Torrecillas asked whether a complete ideal cotorsion pair of object ideals in an exact category always induces a complete cotorsion pair of objects. We show that it need not, even in a Hom-finite, weakly idempotent complete Frobenius exact category. Our example consists of bounded complexes of finite-dimensional vector spaces with even total cohomology dimension. We characterize special object approximations by parity and identify the obstruction as a non-split idempotent in the stable category. For cohereditary pairs, a criterion of Saor\'{\i}n and \v{S}\v{t}ov\'{\i}\v{c}ek gives an affirmative answer when the stable category is idempotent complete.
item.dc:creator: Junpeng Ren, Yucheng Wang

item.title: The rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over F2 is 23
item.description: arXiv:2610.11823v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The rank of the tensor of $3\times 3$ matrix multiplication over the field with two elements is at most $23$ by Laderman's algorithm, and Rudich and Rousseau recently proved that it is at least $22$. We prove that it equals $23$. Hence Laderman's algorithm uses the fewest multiplications among all bilinear algorithms over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and among all bilinear algorithms with integer coefficients. The proof uses the substitution method in the form developed by D'Ambrosio, Wang and Yang et al., which bounds the number of first factors of a decomposition that lie in a given subspace of the space of first factors. We sharpen these bounds for $111$ of Wang's $496$ classes of subspaces, constrain the ranks of the first factors through a $27\times 27$ flattening of the tensor, and list, up to symmetry, all sets of $22$ first factors that satisfy these constraints. An exact completion search shows that none of them is the set of first factors of a decomposition. The computation emits certificates, which are checked in the Lean 4 proof assistant. In one formal proof the largest checks are evaluated as compiled code, and in a second one the kernel evaluates every check, so that its final theorem depends only on the three standard axioms of Lean. The Lean proofs build on the formalization of Rudich and Rousseau and import their table of bounds and their reduction for block algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Tejasvi Singh Tomar
